_meta.indication: EMPLICITI is indicated in combination with lenalidomide and dexamethasone for the treatment of patients with multiple myeloma who have received one to three prior therapies.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label, multicenter trial; patients randomized 1:1 to elotuzumab + lenalidomide/dexamethasone (E-Ld) versus lenalidomide/dexamethasone (Ld).
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with multiple myeloma who had received one to three prior therapies and had documented progression following their most recent therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints of progression-free survival (PFS) and overall response rate (ORR), both assessed by the independent review committee (IRC).
pivotal_trials.n: N=646 randomized; 321 to E-Ld and 325 to Ld.
pivotal_trials.result: PFS HR 0.70 [95% CI 0.57, 0.85], stratified log-rank p=0.0004; median PFS 19.4 months vs 14.9 months. ORR 252 (78.5%) vs 213 (65.5%), p=0.0002.

nct_ctgov.title: Phase III Study of Lenalidomide and Dexamethasone With or Without Elotuzumab to Treat Relapsed or Refractory Multiple Myeloma

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=20%): fatigue, diarrhea, pyrexia, constipation, cough, peripheral neuropathy, nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infection, decreased appetite, pneumonia. Warnings include infusion reactions (~10% of patients), infections, second primary malignancies (9.1% E-Ld vs 5.7% Ld), and hepatotoxicity. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 65.4% (EMPLICITI) vs 56.5% (control).
target_moa: Elotuzumab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds SLAMF7 on myeloma cells and NK cells, directly activating NK cells and recruiting circulating NK cells to the vicinity of the myeloma cell.

rems.type: FDA determined that a REMS is not necessary for elotuzumab to ensure that its benefits outweigh its risks.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the biologic.

description.text: Revised dosing to allow a faster infusion rate up to 5 mL/min and added overall survival data

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for revisions to US Prescribing Information (USPI) Section 2 Dosage and Administration to allow a faster infusion rate for the administration of elotuzumab up to 5 mL/min based on data from CA204112, entitled “*A Phase 2 Single Arm Study of Safety of Elotuzumab Administered over Approximately 60 Minutes in Combination with Lenalidomide and Dexamethasone for Newly Diagnosed or Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma Patients.*” In addition, it provides revisions to USPI Section 14 Clinical Studies to add data for overall survival based on pre-planned interim analysis for study CA204004, entitled “*A Phase 3, Randomized, Open Label Trial of Lenalidomide/dexamethasone With or Without Elotuzumab in Relapsed or Refractory Multiple Myeloma.*”

description.text: Added new indication for Empliciti in combination with pomalidomide and dexamethasone for adults with multiple myeloma after at least two prior therapies including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for a new indication for **Empliciti®** in combination with pomalidomide and dexamethasone for the treatment of adult patients with multiple myeloma who have received at least two prior therapies including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor.

summary.text: Elotuzumab received Breakthrough Therapy Designation (12-May-2014) and priority review, and was granted regular approval based on the phase 3 pivotal trial CA204004 showing improved PFS and ORR with E-Ld versus Ld.

This conclusion is based on the results of the phase 3, pivotal trial CA204004, which evaluated elotuzumab in combination with lenalidomide and dexamethasone (E-Ld) compared with lenalidomide and dexamethasone alone (Ld).
